sampling_model.units: The observed records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with unknown Hölder propensity \(\pi\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The proposed target-fiber mechanism profiles over the full propensity and control-regression Hölder classes; no named nuisance estimator and no fixed finite nuisance sieve is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 establish the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE minimax rate, with the upper construction in Section 5.
Section 4 uses treated--control occupancy and effect homogeneity to obtain a global nonprivate rate with a collision term.
The paper stabilizes central-private U-statistics using local Hájek projections and tuple reweighting.
Section 4 gives a general pure-private T-mechanism based on clipped likelihood-ratio tests and finite covers.
The paper gives central-private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad inequalities based on expected Hamming transport.
Theorems 1 and 3 give finite-query and functional observational CATE releases under approximate differential privacy.
The sparse-histogram lower bound and compact dense-histogram theorem show that pure-private costs can change with representation and occupancy.
Theorems 1--2 and the adaptive lower bound characterize extra logarithmic costs for pointwise federated-private density adaptation.
The paper establishes nonprivate heterogeneous-effect minimax rates with explicit random-design geometry.
Definition 2 and Section 4 construct T-estimators from coherent tests on countable model nets.

body.tldr: Pointwise CATE estimation over the unknown-propensity Hölder model has a nonprivate nuisance-smoothness elbow, while pure privacy creates a second transition governed by observations per localization cell. The proposed occupancy-weighted pair score has constant replacement sensitivity and signal proportional to \(n h^d\min\{1,n\ell^d\}\), so its sparse collision branch and dense first-order branch meet at \(n\ell^d\asymp1\). The central open step is to lift this identity from signed diagnostic mixtures to all target fibers without paying nuisance-sieve entropy. An affirmative lift yields the matched full-class frontier \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\).

project_justification.gap: No located result gives a pure-central-DP minimax frontier for pointwise CATE with unknown smooth propensity and outcome regression. The closest banked construction uses only exactly-two-record cells and therefore loses all signal when cell occupancy diverges.
project_justification.niche: Realized cell occupancy can amplify a degenerate nuisance-product signal while preserving constant record influence, potentially joining the sparse \(n^2\epsilon\) branch to the dense \(n\epsilon\) branch with no third radius.
project_justification.fill: The project isolates the exact occupancy identity, derives a same-class lower frontier, and reduces full-class attainment to a nuisance-independent weighted-shell certificate for occupancy-weighted Hoeffding projections.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman derive the nonprivate Hölder pointwise-CATE frontier and a localized higher-order R-learner; the present target adds pure-private sparse and dense branches on its exact-uniform two-scale specialization. Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy supply the conditioning-on-counts idea for a global discrete-covariate causal estimator, but do not privatize localized nuisance-product projections. Chaudhuri, Loh, Pandey, and Sarkar stabilize private U-statistics through local Hájek projections; their generic kernel theory informs the sensitivity step rather than establishing a CATE fiber theorem. Birgé's Definition 2 supplies the coherent-test architecture for scalar target fibers. Asi, Duchi, Haque, Li, and Ruan convert stable tests into pure-private estimators, but their general cover analysis does not furnish entropy-free full CATE-fiber scores. Acharya, Sun, and Zhang provide the Hamming-coupling converse used to certify both privacy branches. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel release orthogonal CATE queries with Gaussian perturbations under approximate privacy, a distinct privacy model without a minimax Hölder frontier. Balcer and Vadhan show why sparse and dense pure-private representations can obey different error laws. Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen provide the one-shot multiscale and adaptive-lower-bound templates for the follow-on adaptation question. Gao and Han clarify why random-design geometry can change heterogeneous-effect rates, but their model and estimators are nonprivate.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The identity in Lemma 2 does not itself solve the full-fiber problem. For arbitrary least-favorable priors, the second-order kernel orientation can depend on a growing nuisance profile, and clipping local projections can reintroduce a sieve-size factor. The proposed early kill test is the finite \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\) two-resolution program from the parent archive: impose every replacement-neighbor constraint, increase both occupancy and nuisance-sign dimension, and reject the route if the optimized weighted-shell functional grows with the nuisance dimension after occupancy weighting.
body.honest_scope: The fixed-smoothness exact-uniform model is the primary scope. The occupancy-amplification lemma and same-class lower bound are theorem claims; the nuisance-independent full-fiber score is deliberately exposed as Open-ended Question 1, and the combined upper frontier is conditional on its resolution. Transfer to a merely bounded known design density is not claimed. For fixed \(\epsilon\) and \(q<\gamma\), the proposed frontier reduces to the published nonprivate pointwise-CATE order. Smoothness adaptation is a separate open question rather than part of the fixed-class headline.
